correctness.rationale: Every labeling has uniquely determined two zero-class boundaries. The least A-zero and greatest B-zero force exactly the two indicated marked-weight thresholds; binomial products enumerate all assignments with those boundaries without overlap. The separate proof enumerates the six disjoint weight-three possibilities, excludes all weight-two functions for p>=2, and constructs weight four. A separately implemented adjacency-based exhaustive verifier matches all bivariate coefficients on 419 chain profiles and 12,707,343 vertex labelings; the infinite claim rests on the partition proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: The complete two-variable count distinguishes one-label and two-label assignments for an unrestricted canonical chain-graph family, thereby solving a naturally motivated enumerative problem beyond tree/cycle algorithms and numerical minima. The factorization exploits a genuine extreme-neighborhood structural lemma and gives a polynomial-time algorithm independent of treewidth; its weight-three coefficient and multiplicity classification capture nontrivial sharp boundary behavior. It is neither an isolated sample coefficient nor merely a numerical improvement.
